questions_and_answers.answer: The Federal Reserve as a Lender of Last Resort The Federal Reserve, often referred to as the Fed, serves as the central bank of the United States. One of its critical functions is to act as a lender of last resort. This role primarily involves providing liquidity to financial institutions that are experiencing financial difficulties and cannot secure loans from other sources. The purpose of this function is to prevent the failure of financial institutions that could have adverse effects on the overall economy.
